title: Personal Checking: bank-error and courtesy grounds for refunding a fee
content:
## Scope

This policy governs refunds of fees charged to a Personal Checking account. A fee is refunded in full, never in part, as one refund entry that names the fee and equals that fee's amount.

## The two grounds, checked in this order

**1. Bank error.** A bank-error refund applies when the fee was assessed contrary to the Personal Checking terms, for example a monthly maintenance fee in a cycle where a waiver was met; an overdraft fee beyond the tier's daily combined limit, on an item at or below the per-item de minimis amount, or on a day within the end-of-day de minimis amount; or a fee at an amount other than the tier's figure. A bank-error refund has no time limit and does not count toward any courtesy limit.

**2. Courtesy waiver.** A courtesy refund is a goodwill refund of a correctly assessed fee. It is allowed only when every courtesy gate below holds.

## Courtesy gates (all must hold)

| Gate | Condition | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Fee type | The fee is one of: monthly maintenance fee, paper statement fee, overdraft item fee, returned item fee, extended overdraft fee, overdraft transfer fee, out-of-network ATM fee | The fee entry on the account |
| Fee age | The fee posted no more than the tier's courtesy window in calendar days before the courtesy refund is granted | The fee's posted date |
| Allowance | The customer's count of courtesy refunds in the rolling 365 days is below the tier's courtesy allowance | Courtesy refunds across all of the customer's checking accounts |
| Account status | The account is active when the courtesy refund is granted | The account record |

- **Counting the fee age.** Count calendar days with the day after the fee's posted date as day 1; the refund is allowed while the current date is on or before the fee's posted date plus the courtesy window. The boundary day is still allowed.
- **Counting the allowance.** The rolling 365 days end on the current date and include both ends; each refunded fee counts as one.
- **Tier used.** The tier used for the courtesy allowance and window is the account's tier on the current date.
- **Order when the allowance runs short.** When several fees are eligible and the allowance permits fewer than requested, the most recently posted fees are refunded first, and among fees posted the same day the larger fee first.

## Clauses common to both grounds

- A fee can be refunded at most once.
- A refund recorded as dispute final is written under the electronic dispute process and is not a courtesy refund.
- Requests to refund interest, charged-off balances or another bank's fees are outside this policy.

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

**Fee age boundary, with a hypothetical courtesy window of 45 days:** a fee posted on 2026-04-01 may still receive a courtesy refund on 2026-05-16 (day 45) but not on 2026-05-17 (day 46).

**Allowance running short:** a customer may receive one more courtesy refund and asks for three eligible fees: 31.00 USD posted 2026-06-10, 9.00 USD posted 2026-06-12 and 31.00 USD posted 2026-06-12. The most recent day is 2026-06-12, and on that day the larger fee comes first, so the 31.00 USD fee of 2026-06-12 is the one refunded.

**Bank error outside the courtesy window:** a maintenance fee charged in a cycle where a waiver was met is refunded as a bank error even if it posted long ago; the courtesy window and allowance do not apply to it.

## Points of judgement

- **Wrong reading:** "a courtesy refund can cover half the fee". **Correct basis:** every refund is in full, never in part.
- **Wrong reading:** "a wire fee can be refunded as a courtesy". **Correct basis:** only the seven fee types listed in the gate table are eligible for a courtesy refund.
